kjv: he (Yahweh) came with ten thousands of saints
mine: came from the myriads of holy ones
note: Hebrew ve'atah merivevot qodesh has the preposition min "from"; KJV renders it "with", making the holy ones his escort rather than his point of departure (some emend to a place name, Meribath-kadesh).

kjv: they (the holy ones) sat down at thy feet
mine: they (the holy ones) bow down at your feet
note: The verb tukku (from takah?) is a hapax of uncertain meaning; "sat down" and "bow/follow" are both guesses.

kjv: and let [not] his (Reuben's) men be few
note: Hebrew vihi metav mispar says only "and let his men be a number" (i.e. countable, few); the KJV supplies "not" in italics, reversing the clause into a wish for many.

kjv: let his (Judah's) hands be sufficient for him
mine: with his (Judah's) hands he contends for himself
note: Yadav rav lo: rav may be from riv "contend" or rabab "be much/enough"; both readings are defensible.

mine: the horns of a wild ox
note: Re'em is the aurochs/wild ox; "unicorn" came from the Septuagint monokeros.

mine: Most blessed of sons is Asher
note: Barukh mibbanim most naturally means "blessed above (other) sons"; KJV takes min as "with/by" children.

kjv: Thy (Asher's) shoes [shall be] iron and brass
mine: Your (Asher's) bolts will be iron and bronze
note: Min'al is a bar or bolt of a gate (cf. na'al "lock"), not a shoe (na'al); nechoshet is bronze/copper.

kjv: none like unto the God of Jeshurun
note: MT ka'el yeshurun is vocalized as an absolute noun followed by a vocative; KJV reads it as a construct "God of Jeshurun".

kjv: thine (Israel's) enemies shall be found liars unto thee
mine: Your (Israel's) enemies will cringe before you
note: Niphal of kachash here means to feign submission, come cringing; "found liars" is an over-literal sense of the root "deceive".
